dashboard.label: Alerts — status & demo
dashboard.description: Live alert conditions, recently fired alerts, and how to trigger them.

html.p: Two scheduled alerts run every 5 minutes and email js-csco@proton.me. They also appear under Activity → Triggered Alerts and below — so the demo works even if outbound email isn't configured in the lab.

ul.li: High CPU or Memory (>70%) — any host whose latest CPU% or memory% is above 70%.
Universal Forwarder stopped sending — a host that was sending metrics goes quiet for >10 min.

html.p: Email note: the alert fires regardless, but delivery needs an SMTP relay Splunk can reach (Settings → Server settings → Email settings). See the repo README "Alerts" section.

panel.title: Live — CPU/Memory by site (red = would trigger the >70% alert)

search.query: index=loc1_metrics OR index=london_metrics OR index=berlin_metrics sourcetype=linux:metrics | stats latest(cpu_pct) as "CPU %" latest(mem_used_pct) as "Mem %" latest(host) as Host by site | rename site as Site | eval Status=if('CPU %'>70 OR 'Mem %'>70,"● OVER 70%","ok") | table Site Host "CPU %" "Mem %" Status | sort Site

panel.title: Live — forwarder freshness (red = would trigger the "stopped sending" alert)

search.query: | tstats latest(_time) as last WHERE index=loc1_metrics OR index=london_metrics OR index=berlin_metrics by host | eval "Mins since last"=round((now()-last)/60,1), Status=if('Mins since last'>10,"● STALE (>10m)","ok"), "Last seen"=strftime(last,"%F %T") | rename host as Host | table Host "Last seen" "Mins since last" Status | sort - "Mins since last"
index=_audit action=alert_fired earliest=-24h | rename ss_name as Alert, severity as Severity | table _time Alert Severity | sort - _time

panel.title: How to trigger these (for the demo)

html.p: The dashboard panels above update every 30s, so you can watch a row turn red before the 5-minute scheduled alert even runs. To fire the actual alert (and email) immediately, open the saved search in Search & Reporting → Alerts and click Run.
On any Ubuntu box (ubuntu-london / ubuntu-berlin) — pins every core for 4 minutes, then stops on its own:
html.pre: # each worker self-stops after 240s (orphan-safe). Stop early with: pkill -x yes for i in $(seq $(nproc)); do timeout 240 yes >/dev/null & done; wait
html.p: To spike the Splunk host (site loc1) instead, run the same command on the Splunk box. (A heavy index=* search also raises Splunk CPU, but the yes loop is the reliable way to cross 70%.) Stop the spike any time with pkill -x yes.
html.pre: # if stress-ng is available: timeout 240 stress-ng --vm 1 --vm-bytes 80% --vm-keep # otherwise (allocates ~1.5 GB for 4 min): timeout 240 bash -c 'a=$(head -c 1500000000 /dev/zero | tr "\0" "x"); echo held; sleep 240'
html.p: On an Ubuntu box, stop the UF; the "stopped sending" alert fires after ~10 min, and the freshness panel above turns red sooner:
html.pre: sudo /opt/splunkforwarder/bin/splunk stop # ... demo the alert, then bring it back: sudo /opt/splunkforwarder/bin/splunk start
